strengths: Practical and scalable approach: Utilizing uncalibrated, in-the-wild internet videos to tackle the severe scarcity of annotated indoor 3D data is a highly practical and scalable direction.

Well-designed pipeline: The integration of state-of-the-art 2D and 3D foundation models (Dust3R, SAN, DINOv2) with effective heuristics (such as the 2.8m architectural scale prior) provides a solid blueprint for web-scale 3D data curation.

Robust pre-training design: The proposed voxel-anchored Gaussianization and class-prototype distillation framework elegantly addresses the scale and semantic misalignment of noisy pseudo-labels, outperforming direct supervision on pseudo-labels.

Consistent, model-agnostic gains: The method is validated across three distinct architectures (MonoScene, Symphonies, and EmbodiedOcc) on NYUv2 and Occ-ScanNet, showing consistent improvements, especially under limited-data (few-shot) regimes.
weaknesses: Sensitivity to geometric assumptions: The 2.8-meter wall height prior is crucial for resolving scale ambiguity. However, this assumption might fail in diverse indoor spaces such as high-ceiling lofts, offices, or duplexes. The manuscript would benefit from an analysis of the pipeline's robustness when this architectural assumption is violated.

Inherent noise in pseudo-labels: As shown in Table 1, directly training models with standard supervision on the curated pseudo-labels leads to poor performance (8.41% mIoU). Although this justifies the need for the proposed distillation/pre-training framework, it highlights that the curated dataset itself is highly noisy and cannot be easily utilized outside of the proposed pre-training scheme.

Modest gains with full fine-tuning: While the few-shot results are highly encouraging, the margin of improvement when fine-tuning on the full target datasets is relatively modest (e.g., +0.76% mIoU on the full Occ-ScanNet dataset), suggesting a bottleneck in transferring the web-derived features once sufficient target-domain labels are available.

Lack of computational analysis: Generating 3D reconstructions with Dust3R and semantic segmentations with SAN over 100,000 frames is likely computationally demanding. A discussion regarding the computational costs, time, and GPU hours required for the offline curation pipeline is missing.

strengths: Addresses a critical and practical bottleneck in indoor 3D semantic occupancy prediction: the severe scarcity of annotated 3D data, particularly due to privacy and scanning difficulties in indoor environments.
First work to establish a pipeline for learning indoor 3D semantic occupancy from uncalibrated, in-the-wild internet videos (specifically real estate walkthroughs).
Introduces a robust and model-agnostic feature distillation pre-training framework that successfully circumvents the noisy and misaligned nature of direct pseudo-label supervision.
The 'voxel-anchored Gaussianization' module provides an elegant and lightweight way to bridge the 3D-to-2D modality gap for local feature alignment.

Demonstrates consistent, solid performance improvements across three distinct architectures (MonoScene, Symphonies, and EmbodiedOcc) on standard benchmarks (NYUv2 and Occ-ScanNet), with particularly impressive gains in few-shot/data-scarce scenarios.
weaknesses: The geometry reconstruction relies on a strict heuristic assumption of a 2.8-meter wall height to resolve scale ambiguity. This assumption may easily fail in indoor spaces with double-height ceilings, lofts, or public buildings, potentially introducing systematic scaling errors.

Highly dependent on the failure modes of upstream foundation models (Dust3R, SAN, and DINOv2). Errors such as poor reconstruction of thin structures or open-vocabulary segmentation mistakes will inevitably propagate into the pre-training representation.

For the intra-frame region loss (Eq. 2) and prototype loss (Eq. 3), contrastive learning is conducted over only C classes (where C=11). Contrastive learning with such a small number of negative samples can sometimes be unstable or lead to representation collapse; more details or discussion on this limitation would be beneficial.
The computational cost and processing time associated with running Dust3R, SAN, and DINOv2 over 100,000+ frames to generate the YouTube-Occ dataset are not clearly discussed.

strengths: The paper tackles a critical and practical bottleneck in indoor 3D semantic occupancy prediction: the severe scarcity of annotated 3D data and the high cost/privacy concerns of manual annotations.
The idea of leveraging uncalibrated, in-the-wild YouTube videos (specifically real estate footage) is highly creative and offers a scalable alternative to standard sensor-acquired datasets.

The proposed pre-training framework is model-agnostic and utilizes a dual-alignment strategy (intra-frame regional alignment and cross-scene prototype alignment) that effectively mitigates the geometric and semantic noise in pseudo-labels.

Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks (NYUv2 and Occ-ScanNet) across three mainstream architectures (MonoScene, Symphonies, EmbodiedOcc) demonstrate consistent improvements, particularly under data-scarce (few-shot) scenarios.
weaknesses: The heuristic assumption of a 2.8-meter wall height prior to resolve scale ambiguity is quite restrictive. It might fail on indoor scenes with high ceilings (e.g., double-height living rooms, lofts, gymnasiums) or irregular architectural layouts, leading to deformed voxelization during training.

In Section 4.2, the opacity of the Gaussian primitives is predicted via an MLP. It is unclear how this MLP is supervised and stabilized during pre-training without direct depth or RGB reconstruction losses. Clarifying this optimization process is essential for reproducibility.

While the dataset contains over 100k frames, the final improvements under full downstream fine-tuning are somewhat modest (around +1.0% to +1.9% mIoU). Given the heavy computational pipeline involved in processing 100k frames (running Dust3R, SAN, and DINOv2), a cost-benefit or training efficiency analysis is lacking.

The baseline 'Direct 3D Projection' in Table 6 is not fully detailed. It is important to clarify how voxel features are mapped to 2D in this baseline (e.g., projection of voxel centers, bilinear grid sampling, etc.) to better understand the true technical advantage of the Gaussianization module.

strengths: Exploring the use of in-the-wild indoor house tour videos from YouTube for 3D semantic occupancy pre-training is a highly practical and interesting research direction.

A complete pipeline is presented that successfully combines recent geometric (Dust3R) and semantic (SAN) visual foundation models to construct 3D occupancy labels from unannotated RGB videos without requiring camera intrinsics or extrinsics.
The region-level contrastive distillation technique aligns 2D superpixel representations with 3D supervoxels, encouraging the occupancy network to capture object-level semantic consistency.
weaknesses: No Dataset Release: The paper explicitly states that the YouTube-Occ dataset will not be released to the public. This significantly limits the scientific impact and reproducibility of the paper, as other researchers cannot utilize or verify the pre-trained data.

Limited Dataset Scale: With only 14,592 frames from 651 video clips, the scale of YouTube-Occ is quite small for a web-harvested dataset intended for self-supervised pre-training. Many indoor datasets (even the raw sequences of NYUv2 or ScanNet) already contain comparable or larger quantities of frames.

Marginal Performance Improvements: The improvements over the baseline occupancy network (Symphonies) are very slim. On NYUv2, the mIoU increases by only +1.04% (from 29.70% to 30.74%), and on the larger OccScanNet, the improvement is merely +0.30% (from 57.85% to 58.15%). The practical value of the costly pre-training pipeline is therefore questionable.

Poor Zero-Shot Quality: The zero-shot performance when trained purely on YouTube-Occ is extremely low (9.95% mIoU on NYUv2 and 4.61% mIoU on OccScanNet), indicating that the pseudo-ground truths generated by the pipeline suffer from severe domain gap or high geometric/semantic noise.

Absence of Ablation Studies: The paper lacks essential ablation studies. It is unclear how much the 2D visual priors (DINOv2 vs. SAN) contribute, how the superpixel-level contrastive loss performs relative to standard point/pixel-level alignment, or how sensitive the model is to the post-processing heuristics (e.g., assuming a fixed 2.8m wall height).

Writing and Section Referencing Errors: In Section 4, the text incorrectly references Section 3.1 and 3.2 for the method details instead of Section 4.1 and 4.2. Additionally, the index in the contrastive distillation loss equation is inconsistent (summing from 0 to Q, whereas superpixel indices are defined from 1 to Q).

strengths: Exploring the use of in-the-wild YouTube house-tour videos for indoor 3D semantic occupancy prediction is an interesting and practical direction, offering a scalable alternative to expensive manual annotations.

The data processing pipeline is logically designed, integrating Dust3R for camera and depth estimation, visual foundation models (SAN) for semantic labeling, and heuristic filtering/metric scaling to construct the dataset without pre-existing camera parameters.
The proposed object-level pre-training method utilizes 2D region masks to construct superpixels and matching 3D supervoxels, facilitating semantically consistent feature distillation.
weaknesses: The size of the collected YouTube-Occ dataset is quite small (14,592 frames from 651 clips). This is relatively modest for a pre-training dataset and somewhat undermines the claim of being a 'large-scale' web-data learning framework.

The paper states that 'the YouTube-OCC dataset will not be released in public' (Section 6). Given that the dataset is a major declared contribution of the paper, not releasing it greatly limits the reproducibility and the contribution to the broader community.

The quantitative improvements on downstream benchmarks with 100% labeled data are very marginal: only +1.04% mIoU on NYUv2 (Table 1) and +0.30% mIoU on OccScanNet (Table 2) compared to the base Symphonies model.

The zero-shot evaluation performance is very low (9.95% mIoU on NYUv2 and 4.61% on OccScanNet), indicating that the pseudo-annotations generated by the pipeline suffer from severe domain gap or noise issues.

The rough heuristic of scaling the scene by assuming a wall height of 2.8 meters is prone to significant geometric errors in indoor scenes with varied architecture (e.g., high ceilings, lofts), which can degrade spatial predictions.

strengths: The paper addresses a very practical and important problem: the lack of large-scale annotated 3D data for indoor semantic occupancy prediction.
The proposed automated pipeline leveraging Dust3R for camera parameter estimation and SAN for semantic segmentation is a neat way to extract pseudo-annotations from uncalibrated monocular videos.
The VFM-assisted distillation method provides a reasonable framework to align 2D foundation model representations with 3D networks using region-level superpixels.
weaknesses: Non-disclosure of the dataset: The authors state in both the main text (Section 6) and the paper checklist that they will not release the collected YouTube-Occ dataset to the public. Since the dataset is a major portion of the paper's title and claimed contributions, not releasing it severely limits the reproducibility and the scientific value of this work to the research community.

Limited utility of the YouTube-Occ dataset: According to the experimental results, self-supervised pre-training on the target dataset itself (NYUv2) consistently outperforms pre-training on YouTube-Occ. Specifically, at 10% label fraction on NYUv2, pre-training on NYUv2 achieves 22.68% mIoU (Figure 5), whereas pre-training on YouTube-Occ achieves 21.64% mIoU (Table 3). At 100% label fraction, in-domain pre-training gets 30.74% mIoU (Table 1) vs 30.64% mIoU for YouTube-Occ (Table 3). This indicates that the domain gap or reconstruction noise in YouTube-Occ outweighs the benefit of its larger size, undermining the necessity of this external dataset.

Modest dataset scale: The dataset contains only 14,592 frames from 651 video clips. Calling this 'large-scale' is somewhat exaggerated, especially when compared to existing standard datasets like OccScanNet (45,755 training frames) or other web-scale video datasets.

Technical novelty of the distillation method: The concept of projecting 2D features into 3D space and performing contrastive distillation using superpixel/supervoxel clustering is highly similar to prior works such as SLidR (Sautier et al., CVPR 2022). The integration of SAN masks as superpixels is a minor modification.
